title: Test: the limit applied, and the reaction reached, depend on the mode or direction in which the condition occurs

standards_mappings.reference: SYS.4 (system integration testing) and SYS.5 (system verification)
standards_mappings.rationale: This measure is the verification the system requirement states as needed. Its oracle is declared and distinguishable and its execution status is declared; neither constitutes evidence that the requirement is met.

Verification of the system requirement as written, against its own acceptance criteria. The requirement carries a reconstructed ASIL allocation in the reference project; this measure verifies the requirement's behaviour and asserts nothing about whether that allocation is correct.

lifecycle_status_note: Set to the value above because no human has reviewed or approved this record. automated_review_status below refers to corpus automation (schema, link, provenance and consistency checks run by docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py) and is not a statement about engineering validity, organisational independence or human confirmation.

revision_history.author: verification_engineer
revision_history.description: Authored because FB2-SYS-SYR-000004 had no verification, and because its verification approach is declared analysis rather than test, so the measure that suits it is one that reads branching out of the source and exercises it only where exercising is possible.

objective: Confirm that FB2-SYS-SYR-000004's core claim is falsifiable against the pinned source: that the limit applied and the reaction reached are selected by the mode or direction rather than fixed. Two independent mechanisms in the source select on mode or direction. SOA_CheckTemperatures chooses between a discharge tier set and a charge tier set from the sign of the string current, so the same temperature passes or fails depending on direction. The application's state machine selects the contactor reaction from the item's own state and from the requests allowed in that state, and BMS_CheckStateRequest refuses an initialisation request outside the uninitialised state. Both are read from the pinned source and both can be falsified without running the item.
preconditions: The reference project's limit configuration is loaded.
The application's state machine is initialised in the uninitialised state.

environment.hardware: POSIX host (Linux) running the unit-test build, with the SOA module and the application's state machine linked and the diagnosis handler stubbed to record entries
environment.software: foxBMS 2 application firmware built with the unit-test configuration

stimuli.value: positive and negative, in separate cycles
a value that is inside the charge tier set and outside the discharge tier set
an initialisation request issued once in the uninitialised state and once after initialisation

steps.action: Inject the chosen cell temperature with a positive string current and record the entries raised.
steps.expected: The entries raised are the charge-direction temperature entries.

steps.action: Inject the identical temperature with a negative string current.
steps.expected: The entries raised are the discharge-direction temperature entries, which differ from step 1 for at least one tier.

steps.action: Issue an initialisation request in the uninitialised state and record the returned result.
Issue the identical request after initialisation and record the returned result.
steps.expected: The request is refused with a reason specific to the state it was issued in.

steps.action: Record which state the refusal reason came from.
steps.expected: The refusal is attributable to the state rather than to a fixed policy.

oracle_detail.why_this_oracle: The oracle is the branching the pinned source performs. The temperature path contains an explicit test of the current's sign that selects between two threshold sets, and the request path contains an explicit test of the current state that returns one of several distinct refusal values. Both are properties of code that exists, readable at the pinned commit, and falsifiable by changing one condition in either.
oracle_detail.what_the_oracle_is_not: It is not a measured reference: neither branch was exercised by a run in this authoring pass. It is not an analytical model: no timing or magnitude arithmetic is involved. It is not a synthetic assumption: the branching is in the source.
oracle_detail.what_it_still_does_not_prove: It does not prove the reference project's reaction set per mode is the right set, that no mode is missing, or that the published mode reaches the vehicle control unit within the publication period the requirement also demands. The publication half of FB2-SYS-SYR-000004 is verified by a different mechanism and is not claimed here.
oracle_detail.residual_risk: Two mechanisms are checked that are not the one the requirement names. The requirement asks for reaction selected by mode; the source selects temperature limits by current direction and initialisation requests by state. Whether current direction is the reference project's notion of mode is an interpretation, and this record states the interpretation rather than hiding it.

cleanup: Reset the state machine to the uninitialised state, restore the stubbed diagnosis handler, and confirm the limit configuration is unchanged.
regression_selection: Re-run on every change to the temperature tier selection, to the request admissibility rules, to the application's state enumeration, or on any addition of a mode. Also re-run whenever a mode is added, because this measure can only check the modes the code actually branches on and a new mode is exactly the case it would miss.
limitations: This measure checks that reaction selection depends on direction and on state. It does not check the requirement's mode-publication criterion, which needs a vehicle-control-unit interface this corpus does not have.
The identification of current direction with the requirement's notion of mode is an interpretation stated in the record, not a finding.
Nothing has been executed. The paired execution record carries execution_kind 'none' and outcome 'blocked'.
This is a synthetic measure for the hypothetical reference project.
